reader.decision_reason: The message traces the double send to `digest-builder` running from both cron and the Kubernetes CronJob, and the unchecked cutover step is the root cause. Removing the line costs one line and breaks no code, while both of my proposed fixes only mask the duplicate run.

reconstruction.problem: `digest-builder` runs twice every Monday at 06:00 UTC, once from the `ops-box-2` crontab and once from the Kubernetes CronJob. Each run inserts one pending `outbox` row per active subscriber (18412), so the table holds 36824 rows. `outbox` has no unique constraint, and `send_pending` sends every pending row, so each subscriber gets the digest twice.
reconstruction.what_breaks: Every subscriber receives the Monday digest twice. `concurrencyPolicy: Forbid` does not help because it cannot see the cron run on `ops-box-2`. The cutover checklist item 'Remove the digest_builder line' was left unchecked. My two proposed fixes, mailer dedupe by email and a unique index, only hide the duplicate run. Mailer dedupe also leaves 18412 extra rows in `outbox` every week and drops legitimate rows when two subscribers share an address.
reconstruction.fix: Delete line 3 (`0 6 * * 1 ... jobs.digest_builder`) from `ops/hosts/ops-box-2/crontab`, keep line 2 (`rotate-logs`), and tick the checklist item in `docs/migrations/2026-09-k8s-cutover.md`. If the repo file is a copy of the live crontab, edit the live crontab on `ops-box-2` too. Add the unique index on `outbox(subscriber_id, digest_date)` later as a backstop.
reconstruction.cost: The crontab removal costs one line and breaks no code. The later unique index costs more: existing duplicate rows must be deleted first, and the `INSERT` at `jobs/digest_builder.py:7` needs `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` or the second run crashes on a unique violation. It becomes the primary fix if the builder must stay on two schedulers.
